full_judgment: 3. The petitioners are owners and possessors of land situated Umpanpur Mouza, Upazila Jiantapur, District Sylhet at Dag No. 204 land 0.05 acre, Dag No. 206, land 0.31 acre, Dag No. 214, land 0.63 acre, Dag No. 207, land 0.29 acre, Dag No. 209, land 0.26 acre, Dag No. 21.0, land 0.61 acre, Dag No. 216, land 0.50 acre, Dag No. 213, land 0.23 acre, Dag No. 215, land 0.25 acre, Dag No. 217 part, land 0.50 acre, Dag No. 221, land 0.55 acre, Dag No. 222, land 0.22 acre, Dag No. 223, land 0.13 acre corresponding to khatian Nos. 49,120,116, 53, 47, 42, 59, 95 11, 99, 978 in total measuring about 4.53 acre of land were acquired by respondents under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. 11 of 1982) for Sylhet Gas Fields Ltd. The respondent No. 8 vide his letter being Memo No. জেপ্রসি/এল.এ/২০০৭-২৯০ dated 09.09.2007 appointed Kanungo and Government Surveyor for joint survey, video recording and infra-structure of the proposed acquired site of the petitioners and others and a report thereof was directed to submit on 10.09.2007 at 11:00 A. M. Thereafter, the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, District-Sylhet/ respondent No. 8 on behalf of the Sylhet Gas Field Ltd. by L.A. Case No.12/ 2006-2007 acquired those immovable properties of the petitioners and others for establishing an oil drill well/oil deep basin in Umpanpur Mouia, Upazila Jiantapur, District-Sylhet. Thereafter, L.A. Officer/respondent No. 8 issued a letter being Memo No. জেপ্রসি/এল.এ/২০০৭-২৯০-৩১৯/১(৩) dated 22.10.2007 to collect list Of deed of sale and purchase of lands from Sub-registry relating to Umpanpur Mouza, Upazila Jiantapur, District-Sylhet from 03.09.2006 to 02.09.2007. Accordingly, the immovable/lands of the petitioners and others were acquired by the Government of Bangladesh/respondent Nos. 6, 8 on behalf of Sylhet Gas Fields Ltd. under the aforesaid Ordinance. The petitioners and others for the greater interest of the country and the people did not raise any objection to such acquisition. Accordingly, the respondents issued notices under Section 3 of the said Ordinance to the petitioner and others and invited objection, if any, from them. The respondents without having found any objection from the petitioner and others issued 11 notices under Section 6 of the said Ordinance and thus invited written statement of interest about the proposed acquisition of the land/ immovable properties of the petitioner and others in L.A Case No. 12/2006-2007 dated 02.10.2007. The petitioner and others in the hope of getting justice and adequate compensation value/price of their proposed acquired land did not raise any objection to such acquisition under Sections 3 and 6 of the said Ordinance and were waiting for the award notices under Section 7 of the said Ordinance which were finally issued on 26.02.2008 under Section 7 of the said Ordinance in which is found that the respondent without observing the procedure mentioned under Section 8(1)(a) of the said Ordinance fixed up award/compensation value/price at a price which is far below the value /price as per Section 8(1)(a) of the Ordinance. The petitioners and others having received the aforesaid award notices as mentioned in Annexure-B series above got very much shocked and astonished because of the price of per decimal of land fixed by the respondents. As a result, the petitioners sent a demand jus-tice notice on 28.02.2008 through their lawyer praying for reassessment of the compensation by the respondents can-celling the said award notices under Section 7 of the said Ordinance but until now no reply was received from the respondents. Thereafter, the petitioners on 02.03.2008 filed objection against the assessment of award/compensation at such a low rate per decimal of land which was duly received by the respondent No. 8. But until now no reply to such objection or demand of justice notice given by the respondents. The petitioners on 02.03.2008 applied for certified copies of the entire proceedings of the L.A. Case No. 12/2006-2007 but the respondents with malafide intention did not supply the certified copies of the entire proceedings. The respondents are required to re-assess/give award/compensation for the acquired land owners as per Section 8(1)(a) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. 11 of 1982). The petitioners collected and confirmed with the respondents No. 9 that the total 6(six) deeds of sale and purchase with similar description and similar advantages have been examined and calculated by the respondents in assessing the award as being Deed No. 2329/06 dated 14.12.2006, Deed No. 2300/06 dated 13.12.2006, Deed No. 2302/06 dated 13.12.2006, Deed No. 1790/06 dated 14.09.2006, Deed No .2027 dated 08.11.2006 and Deed No. 2083/06 dated 15.11.2006 examined and calculated in assessing the award/compensation of the value of per decimal of land of the petitioners.
